questions.question: A student wrote the ionic equation Ag2+(l) + 2Cl-(l) gives AgCl2(s) for the precipitation of silver chloride. Explain why this equation is incorrect even though it is balanced.
questions.answer: Silver is Ag+, not Ag2+, and silver chloride is AgCl, not AgCl2; correct ionic equation is Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq) gives AgCl(s)
steps: Silver forms the common ion Ag+ (one electron lost), so Ag2+ has the wrong charge
Silver chloride contains Ag+ and Cl- in a 1:1 ratio, so the formula is AgCl, and AgCl2 would need Ag2+
The equation balances only because the wrong charges and formula were chosen consistently
Correct ionic equation: Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq) gives AgCl(s), with state symbols for the ions in solution and the precipitate as solid

questions.question: A compound contains 3.09 g C, 0.26 g H and 9.15 g Cl. Its molar mass is 97.0 g mol-1. Find its molecular formula.
questions.answer: C2H2Cl2
steps: Divide by the smallest (0.2575): C : H : Cl = 1 : 1 : 1, so empirical formula CHCl
Empirical formula mass = 12.0 + 1.0 + 35.5 = 48.5 g mol-1
n = 97.0/48.5 = 2, so the molecular formula is (CHCl)2 = C2H2Cl2

questions.question: Nitrogen trichloride NCl3 contains only 14N and chlorine atoms of mass 35 and 37. Give the formula and m/z of the four molecular ion peaks.
steps: The molecular ion is [NCl3]+; its mass depends on which chlorine isotopes are present
Mass of N = 14; each 35Cl adds 35 and each 37Cl adds 37
All three 35Cl: 14 + 105 = 119; two 35Cl and one 37Cl: 121; one 35Cl and two 37Cl: 123; all 37Cl: 125
Give the four ions with their m/z values as listed in the answer

questions.question: Complete the table to predict the shape and Cl-N-Cl bond angle of nitrogen trichloride. The table is not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: 3 bonding pairs; 1 lone pair; trigonal pyramidal; Cl-N-Cl about 107 degrees
steps: N has 5 outer electrons: 3 are shared with three Cl atoms, leaving 2 electrons as one lone pair
So there are 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, four electron pairs in total
Four pairs arrange tetrahedrally, but only three point at atoms, so the shape is trigonal pyramidal
The lone pair repels the bonding pairs more than they repel each other, squeezing the angle to about 107 degrees (less than 109.5)

questions.question: Explain why solid aluminium chloride, which is ionic, has significant covalent character.
questions.answer: The small, highly charged Al3+ ion has high charge density, so it polarises the large Cl- ion and distorts its electron cloud
steps: Al3+ is small and has a 3+ charge, so its charge density is high
High charge density polarises the large, easily distorted Cl- anion
Polarisation draws the electron density of Cl- towards Al3+, giving the Al-Cl bond shared-electron (covalent) character

questions.question: Describe how two AlCl3 molecules are joined in the dimer Al2Cl6, including a diagram.
questions.answer: Each AlCl3 has an empty orbital on Al; a lone pair on a Cl of the other molecule forms a dative covalent bond to Al, giving two bridging Cl atoms
steps: Each Al in AlCl3 has only 6 electrons, so it is electron deficient and has an empty orbital
A chlorine atom on one molecule uses a lone pair to form a dative covalent bond to Al of the other molecule
Two such bridging Cl atoms link the two Al atoms, giving a four-membered Al2Cl2 ring with Cl bridges
Diagram: draw two AlCl3 units with two bridging Cl atoms, each Cl bonded to both Al atoms, with an arrow from the bridging Cl to Al for the dative bonds

questions.question: Which species is not tetrahedral? The answer options are missing from the extracted text.
questions.answer: C: ICl4^-
steps: CCl4, CH4 and NH4^+ each have four bonding pairs and no lone pairs on the central atom, so all are tetrahedral
In ICl4^- iodine has 7 outer electrons + 1 from the charge + 4 from Cl = 6 pairs: 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs
Six pairs point octahedrally with the two lone pairs opposite each other, so the ion is square planar, not tetrahedral

questions.question: Complete the electronic configuration of phosphorus (atomic number 15) using electrons-in-boxes notation.
questions.answer: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3, with the three 3p electrons in separate boxes (one each)
steps: Phosphorus has 15 electrons: 2 in 1s, 2 in 2s, 6 in 2p, 2 in 3s and 3 in 3p
The 3p subshell has three boxes; by Hund's rule, the three electrons go into separate boxes with parallel spins
Result: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p3 with three unpaired electrons

questions.question: Explain why the first ionisation energy of phosphorus is greater than that of sulfur.
questions.answer: P has a half-filled, stable 3p3 subshell; S removes an electron from a 3p4 orbital that is destabilised by repulsion between paired electrons
steps: Phosphorus 3p3 has a half-filled subshell, which is extra stable
Sulfur 3p4 has one orbital with two paired electrons, so they repel each other
The electron removed from sulfur is therefore easier to lose, so its ionisation energy is lower

questions.question: Phosphorus melts at 44 degrees C and silicon at 1410 degrees C. Explain why phosphorus has a much lower melting temperature.
questions.answer: Phosphorus is simple molecular with weak van der Waals forces between molecules; silicon is giant covalent with many strong covalent bonds to break
steps: Phosphorus exists as small discrete P4 molecules
The forces between these molecules are weak van der Waals (London) forces, which need little energy to overcome
Silicon is a giant covalent lattice in which every atom is joined by strong covalent bonds
Melting silicon requires breaking many strong covalent bonds, so it needs a much higher temperature

questions.question: Complete the table for a PCl5 molecule. The table is not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: 5 bonding pairs; 0 lone pairs; trigonal bipyramidal; Cl-P-Cl angles 90 degrees and 120 degrees
steps: P has 5 outer electrons and forms 5 P-Cl bonds, so it has 5 bonding pairs and 10 electrons in its outer shell
All 5 pairs are bonding pairs, so there are no lone pairs
Five bonding pairs repel equally and are furthest apart as a trigonal bipyramid
Three equatorial Cl are 120 degrees apart; each axial Cl is 90 degrees from the equatorial ones

questions.question: Solid PCl5 is ionic. The cation is tetrahedral and the anion is octahedral, each with one P atom and a different number of Cl atoms. Give the formula and charge of each ion.
questions.answer: Cation PCl4+ (tetrahedral); anion PCl6- (octahedral)
steps: Tetrahedral cation with one P has 4 Cl atoms (4 bonding pairs, no lone pairs)
P has 5 valence electrons; with 4 Cl atoms and one positive charge, the cation is PCl4+
Octahedral anion with one P has 6 Cl atoms (6 bonding pairs), and the extra electron makes it PCl6-

questions.question: 8.00 cm3 of 0.250 mol dm-3 NaOH reacts completely with 10.0 cm3 of 0.100 mol dm-3 H3PO4. Deduce the balanced equation.
questions.answer: 2NaOH + H3PO4 gives Na2HPO4 + 2H2O
steps: Ratio NaOH : H3PO4 = 2 : 1, so two of the three acidic H+ ions are neutralised
Balanced equation: 2NaOH + H3PO4 gives Na2HPO4 + 2H2O

questions.question: Hydrated magnesium phosphate Mg3(PO4)2.yH2O is 78.5% anhydrous Mg3(PO4)2 by mass. Find y. Molar mass of Mg3(PO4)2 = 262.9 g mol-1.
steps: Molar mass of hydrate = 262.9/0.785 = 334.9 g mol-1
Mass of water in one mole of hydrate = 334.9 - 262.9 = 72.0 g
Moles of water = 72.0/18.0 = 4.0
So y = 4

questions.question: How many lone pairs of electrons are in the outer shell of the sulfur atom in H2S? Options: A zero, B one, C two, D four.
questions.answer: C (two lone pairs)
steps: Sulfur has 6 outer electrons
Two of these form S-H bonds (one electron from each atom), using 2 electrons
The remaining 4 electrons form two lone pairs

questions.question: In which sequence are the molecules in order of decreasing bond angle? Options: A BeCl2 > BCl3 > CH4, B BeCl2 > NH3 > CH4, C CH4 > BCl3 > BeCl2, D CH4 > NH3 > BeCl2.
questions.answer: A (BeCl2 180 deg > BCl3 120 deg > CH4 109.5 deg)
steps: BeCl2 is linear with two bonding pairs: 180 degrees
BCl3 is trigonal planar with three bonding pairs: 120 degrees
CH4 is tetrahedral with four bonding pairs: 109.5 degrees
Order: BeCl2 > BCl3 > CH4, which is option A

questions.question: Which molecule is planar? Options: A CF4, B C2F4, C PF5, D SF6.
questions.answer: B (C2F4)
steps: CF4 is tetrahedral and not planar
C2F4 is like ethene: each C has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so it is trigonal planar and flat
PF5 is trigonal bipyramidal and SF6 is octahedral; neither is planar

questions.question: Complete the table for a molecule of NCl3 (molecular structure, shape and bond angle). The table is not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: 3 bond pairs; 1 lone pair; Cl-N-Cl about 107 degrees; trigonal pyramidal
steps: The displayed formula shows three N-Cl single bonds, so there are 3 bonding pairs around N
N has 5 outer electrons, 3 used in bonding, so 2 remain as 1 lone pair
Four electron pairs with one lone pair give a trigonal pyramidal shape
Lone pair-bond pair repulsion is greater than bond pair-bond pair repulsion, so the angle is about 107 degrees

questions.question: Explain why PCl5, a solid of ions, has a higher melting temperature than SbCl5, which is made of molecules.
questions.answer: PCl5 has strong electrostatic attraction between ions in a lattice; SbCl5 has only weak van der Waals forces between molecules
steps: PCl5 is ionic (PCl4+ and PCl6-), held by strong electrostatic attraction in a lattice
Melting PCl5 requires a large amount of energy to overcome these ionic bonds
SbCl5 is molecular, so only weak van der Waals forces between molecules need to be overcome
Less energy is needed, so SbCl5 melts at a lower temperature

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of a molecule of SbCl5, showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: Sb in the centre with five single covalent bonds to five Cl atoms, each bond one shared pair (Sb electron dot, Cl electron cross), no lone pairs on Sb
steps: Sb has 5 outer electrons, each Cl has 7 outer electrons
Each Cl shares one electron with Sb, forming five Sb-Cl single bonds
Sb uses all five outer electrons in bonds, so there are no lone pairs on Sb
Each Cl has three lone pairs (6 electrons) plus the shared pair

questions.question: State what is meant by the term dative covalent bond.
questions.answer: A shared pair of electrons in which both electrons come from the same atom (one atom donates the lone pair)
steps: A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between two atoms
In a dative covalent bond, both electrons of the shared pair come from one atom
The donor atom has a lone pair and the acceptor atom has an empty orbital

questions.question: Complete the diagram to show the dative covalent bonds in Sb2Cl10.
questions.answer: Two bridging Cl atoms, each donating a lone pair to an Sb atom of the other SbCl5 unit (arrows from Cl to Sb)
steps: Sb2Cl10 is two SbCl5 units joined together
Two terminal Cl atoms of one unit each use a lone pair to bond to the Sb of the other unit
Draw an arrow from each bridging Cl to the Sb it bonds to, giving two dative bonds

questions.question: Give one reason why nitrogen does not form a pentachloride, unlike the other Group 5 elements.
questions.answer: Nitrogen has no empty d orbitals in its outer shell, so it cannot expand its octet to form five bonds
steps: Nitrogen is in period 2 with only 2s and 2p orbitals in its outer shell
Five bonds need ten electrons in the outer shell (an expanded octet)
Without d orbitals, nitrogen cannot expand its octet; it is also too small to fit five Cl atoms

questions.topic: Electronic Configuration Of Be And Ca
questions.question: Complete the electronic configurations of beryllium and calcium using s, p, d notation.
steps: Beryllium has 4 electrons: 1s2 2s2
Calcium has 20 electrons: fill 1s2, 2s2, 2p6, 3s2, 3p6, then 4s2
Result: Be 1s2 2s2; Ca 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram showing the bonding in a gaseous molecule of beryllium chloride, BeCl2.
questions.answer: Be in the centre with two single covalent bonds to two Cl atoms, each bond one shared pair; no lone pairs on Be
steps: Be has 2 outer electrons; each Cl has 7
Each Cl shares one electron with Be, forming two Be-Cl bonds
Be uses both its outer electrons in bonds, so there are no lone pairs on Be
Each Cl has three lone pairs plus the shared pair

questions.topic: Dative And Covalent Bonds In BeCl2
questions.question: In solid BeCl2, a polymer uses two types of covalent bond shown by lines and arrows. Describe how each type of bond is formed.
questions.answer: Normal covalent bond: one electron from each atom forms a shared pair. Dative covalent bond: a Cl lone pair is donated to an empty orbital on Be
steps: A normal covalent bond forms when each atom contributes one electron to a shared pair
A dative covalent bond forms when a Cl atom donates a lone pair to an electron-deficient Be atom
In the polymer, the arrows show the dative bonds and the plain lines show normal covalent bonds

questions.question: Predict the Cl-Be-Cl bond angle in gaseous (monomer) BeCl2 and in the solid polymer, justifying each using electron pair repulsion theory.
questions.answer: Monomer: 180 degrees (linear). Polymer: about 109.5 degrees (tetrahedral around each Be)
steps: Monomer BeCl2 has two bonding pairs and no lone pairs on Be
Two bonding pairs repel equally and get maximum separation, so the molecule is linear with a 180 degree angle
In the polymer, each Be is bonded to four Cl atoms (two normal, two dative), with four bonding pairs
Four bonding pairs repel to a tetrahedral arrangement, giving bond angles of about 109.5 degrees

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram for anhydrous calcium chloride, which is ionic, showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: Ca2+ with no outer electrons, and two Cl- ions each with a complete octet (8 electrons), with the Ca electrons transferred to the Cl atoms
steps: Ca has 2 outer electrons and each Cl has 7
Ca transfers one electron to each of two Cl atoms, forming Ca2+ and two Cl-
Each Cl- has a full outer shell of 8 electrons; Ca2+ has none
Draw the ions with square brackets and charges: [Cl]- [Ca]2+ [Cl]-

questions.question: Explain why gaseous beryllium chloride and solid calcium chloride have different types of bonding.
questions.answer: Be2+ is very small with high charge density, so it polarises Cl and gives covalent character; Ca2+ is larger with lower charge density, so bonding is ionic
steps: Be2+ is small and highly charged, so it has high charge density
High charge density distorts (polarises) the electron cloud of Cl, giving shared-electron character
Ca2+ is larger with a lower charge density, so it polarises Cl less
CaCl2 therefore remains largely ionic, held in a lattice by electrostatic attraction

questions.question: Explain what is meant by the term isotopes.
questions.answer: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons (different mass numbers)
steps: Isotopes are atoms of the same element
They have the same number of protons, so the same atomic number
They have different numbers of neutrons, so different mass numbers

questions.topic: Relative Atomic Mass From Mass Spectrum
questions.question: Calculate the relative atomic mass of germanium from the mass spectrum shown. The spectrum is not in the extracted text.
steps: Ar = sum of (mass x abundance) / sum of abundances

questions.question: Give the electronic configuration of a germanium atom (atomic number 32).
steps: Germanium has 32 electrons
Fill in order: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2 3d10 4p2
Write the subshells in order of number: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p2

questions.question: Calculate the atom economy by mass for the formation of GeH4 from Na2GeO3 + NaBH4 + H2O gives GeH4 + 2NaOH + NaBO2. Ar of Ge = 72.6.
steps: Molar mass of GeH4 = 72.6 + 4 x 1.0 = 76.6 g mol-1
Molar masses of reactants: Na2GeO3 = 166.6, NaBH4 = 37.8, H2O = 18.0 (using Ar Na = 23.0, B = 10.8, O = 16.0, H = 1.0); total = 222.4 g mol-1
Atom economy = mass of desired product / total mass of reactants x 100

questions.question: Germane donates a proton to ammonia to form an ion. Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of this ion, showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: GeH3- ion: Ge with three Ge-H bonds and one lone pair, overall charge -1
steps: Germane GeH4 loses one H+ (a proton) to NH3, leaving GeH3-
Ge has 4 outer electrons; the 3 Ge-H bonds use 3 of them, and the H+ lost from GeH4 leaves its bonding pair behind on Ge
So the 8 electrons of the ion are 3 bonding pairs plus 1 lone pair on Ge, and the extra electron gives the -1 charge
Show the ion in square brackets with charge -1

questions.question: Using the answer to (d)(ii) and electron pair repulsion theory, name the shape and give the bond angle of the GeH3- ion.
questions.answer: Trigonal pyramidal; bond angle less than 109.5 degrees
steps: GeH3- has three bonding pairs and one lone pair on Ge
The lone pair repels bonding pairs more strongly than bonding pairs repel each other
The shape is trigonal pyramidal, with H-Ge-H angles less than the tetrahedral 109.5 degrees

questions.question: Germane has a maximum permitted concentration of 0.640 mg m-3 in air. Calculate the maximum number of GeH4 molecules in a laboratory of volume 231 m3. Avogadro constant = 6.02 x 10^23 mol-1.
questions.answer: 1.16 x 10^21 molecules
steps: Mass of GeH4 allowed = 0.640 mg m-3 x 231 m3 = 147.8 mg = 0.1478 g
Molar mass of GeH4 = 76.6 g mol-1, so moles = 0.1478/76.6 = 1.93 x 10^-3 mol
Number of molecules = 1.93 x 10^-3 x 6.02 x 10^23
= 1.16 x 10^21 molecules

questions.question: 335.5 cm3 of CO2 is formed at r.t.p. (molar volume 24 000 cm3 mol-1). Calculate the moles of CO2 formed.
steps: Moles = volume / molar volume
Give to 3 significant figures: 0.0140 mol

questions.question: Deduce the moles of HX formed when GeX4 reacted with excess water, using MgCO3 + 2HX gives MgX2 + CO2 + H2O.
questions.answer: 0.0280 mol HX
steps: From the equation, 2 mol HX react with 1 mol MgCO3 to give 1 mol CO2
So moles of HX = 2 x moles of CO2 = 2 x 0.01398 = 0.0280 mol

questions.question: Deduce the moles of GeX4 that reacted with excess water, given GeX4 + 2H2O gives GeO2 + 4HX.
questions.answer: 0.00699 mol GeX4
steps: From the equation, 1 mol GeX4 gives 4 mol HX
Moles of GeX4 = 0.0280/4 = 0.00699 mol

questions.topic: Molar Mass And Identity Of Halogen
questions.question: 1.50 g of GeX4 reacted with water. Calculate the molar mass of GeX4 and identify X.
questions.answer: Molar mass 214.6 g mol-1; X = Cl (GeCl4)
steps: Molar mass = mass / moles = 1.50 / 0.00699 = 214.6 g mol-1
Mass of 4 X atoms = 214.6 - 72.6 = 142.0 g mol-1, so Ar of X = 142.0/4 = 35.5
Ar 35.5 corresponds to chlorine, so X = Cl and the compound is GeCl4

questions.question: State how vaporised atoms are ionised in a mass spectrometer.
questions.answer: By bombardment with high-energy electrons, which knock out an electron to form positive ions
steps: Vaporised atoms pass through a stream of high-energy electrons
Collision removes an outer electron, giving a positive ion X+

questions.question: State how the ions formed in a mass spectrometer are accelerated.
questions.answer: By an electric field, using accelerating (electrostatic) plates at a high voltage
steps: The positive ions are attracted to a negatively charged plate
An electric field across the accelerating plates gives the ions kinetic energy

questions.question: Explain why isotopes of an element have the same chemical reactions but their ions are deflected differently in a mass spectrometer.
questions.answer: Isotopes have the same electron configuration, so same chemical behaviour; they have different masses, so their ions have different m/z and are deflected differently
steps: Isotopes have the same number of protons and electrons, so the same electronic structure
Chemical reactions depend on electron configuration, which is the same
Isotopes have different masses, so their ions have different mass-to-charge ratios
A magnetic field deflects ions by an amount that depends on m/z, so the isotopes are deflected differently

questions.question: State what is meant by relative atomic mass.
questions.answer: The weighted mean mass of an atom of an element compared with one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom
steps: Relative atomic mass is the average mass of the isotopes of an element, weighted by their abundance
It is compared with one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom, so it has no units

questions.question: A sample of chlorine contains 75.53% 35Cl and 24.47% 37Cl. Calculate its relative atomic mass to four significant figures.
steps: Divide by 100 to get the weighted mean: 35.4894
To 4 significant figures: 35.49

questions.question: Three peaks lie between m/z 101 and 105 in the mass spectrum of PCl3. Complete the table giving the ions responsible. The table is not in the extracted text.
steps: Phosphorus has only 31P, so differences between peaks come from the Cl isotopes
101 = 31 + 35 + 35, so the ion is [31P 35Cl2]+ (two 35Cl atoms)
103 = 31 + 35 + 37, so the ion is [31P 35Cl 37Cl]+
105 = 31 + 37 + 37, so the ion is [31P 37Cl2]+; each ion has charge 1+ (one electron lost in the spectrometer)

questions.question: Show that the relative peak heights in the table are consistent with a 35Cl : 37Cl ratio of 3 : 1. The table values are not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: Probabilities 9/16 : 6/16 : 1/16 = 9 : 6 : 1, matching the peak heights
steps: If 35Cl : 37Cl = 3 : 1, then P(35Cl) = 3/4 and P(37Cl) = 1/4
m/z 103 needs one of each, in either order: 2 x (3/4) x (1/4) = 6/16
m/z 105 needs two 37Cl: (1/4) x (1/4) = 1/16, so the heights are in the ratio 9 : 6 : 1, as in the table

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of a PCl3 molecule, showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: P in the centre with three single bonds to Cl atoms and one lone pair on P; each Cl has three lone pairs
steps: P has 5 outer electrons and each Cl has 7
Each Cl shares one electron with P, forming three P-Cl bonds (three shared pairs)
The remaining two P electrons form one lone pair on P

questions.question: Explain the shape of a PCl3 molecule using electron pair repulsion theory.
questions.answer: Trigonal pyramidal: three bonding pairs and one lone pair; the lone pair repels more strongly, so the Cl-P-Cl angle is less than 109.5 degrees
steps: PCl3 has four electron pairs around P: three bonding pairs and one lone pair
The four pairs arrange tetrahedrally to minimise repulsion
Only the three bonding pairs are seen in the molecular shape, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape
The lone pair repels bonding pairs more than bonding pairs repel each other, pushing the Cl-P-Cl angle below 109.5 degrees

questions.question: Which molecule has the largest bond angle? Options: A BF3, B CF4, C H2O, D NH3.
questions.answer: A (BF3, 120 degrees)
steps: BF3 is trigonal planar with three bonding pairs: 120 degrees
CF4 is tetrahedral: 109.5 degrees
NH3 is trigonal pyramidal: about 107 degrees
H2O is bent with two lone pairs: about 104.5 degrees

questions.question: Explain the general trend in first ionisation energy across Period 2.
questions.answer: First ionisation energy generally increases across Period 2 because nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar, so the outer electrons are held more strongly and atomic radius decreases
steps: Across the period, the nuclear charge increases by one proton per element
Electrons are added to the same shell, so shielding stays similar
The outer electrons feel a greater attraction and the atomic radius decreases
More energy is needed to remove an electron, so the first ionisation energy increases

questions.question: Predict a value for the first ionisation energy of oxygen and justify it. The graph of first ionisation energies is not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: About 1300 kJ mol^-1 (any value between 1086 and 1402), lower than nitrogen
steps: From the table, N is 1402 and C is 1086, and O has two more protons than C, so a value between these is expected
Ignoring electron pairing, the value would be higher than N, in line with the general rise across the period
But in oxygen (2p4) two electrons share one 2p orbital and repel each other
The repulsion between the paired electrons makes one of them easier to remove, so the first ionisation energy dips below that of N (actual value 1314)

questions.question: Write the equation for the second ionisation energy of lithium, including state symbols.
questions.answer: Li+(g) gives Li2+(g) + e-
steps: Second ionisation removes one electron from the 1+ ion
Li+ has lost its first electron; the second ionisation gives Li2+ and one electron
Both species are gases: Li+(g) gives Li2+(g) + e-

questions.question: Explain the large difference between the first and second ionisation energies of lithium (second is 7298 kJ mol-1).
questions.answer: The second electron is removed from the full, inner 1s shell, which is close to the nucleus and strongly held, so much more energy is needed
steps: Lithium's first electron is removed from the 2s subshell, which is outside the full 1s shell
After this, Li2+ has a full 1s2 shell, so the second electron comes from a stable, full inner shell
The inner shell is close to the nucleus and well shielded from outer electrons, so it is held very strongly

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of the molecule BeCl2, showing outer electrons.
questions.answer: Be in the centre with two single bonds to two Cl atoms, each Cl with three lone pairs; no lone pairs on Be
steps: Be has 2 outer electrons, each Cl has 7
Each Cl shares one electron with Be, giving two Be-Cl bonds
Be has no lone pairs, and each Cl has three lone pairs

questions.question: Explain the shape and bond angle of the BeCl2 molecule.
questions.answer: Shape: linear. Bond angle: 180 degrees. Explanation: two bonding pairs on Be repel each other equally and get maximum separation
steps: Be has two bonding pairs and no lone pairs around it
Two electron pairs repel each other as far apart as possible
They point in opposite directions, so the molecule is linear
The Cl-Be-Cl bond angle is 180 degrees

questions.question: Draw a diagram showing two BeCl2 molecules bonding together to form the dimer Be2Cl4, and state the type of bond involved.
questions.answer: Two bridging Cl atoms, each donating a lone pair to the Be of the other molecule; bond type: dative covalent
steps: Each Be in BeCl2 is electron deficient, with an empty orbital
A Cl atom on one molecule donates a lone pair to the Be of the other molecule
Two such bridging Cl atoms form a four-membered Be2Cl2 ring
Diagram: draw two BeCl2 units joined by two Cl bridges with arrows from Cl to Be; the bond type is dative covalent

questions.question: Which molecule has the largest bond angle? Options: A BCl3, B CO2, C H2O, D NH3.
questions.answer: B (CO2, 180 degrees)
steps: CO2 is linear with two bonding regions: 180 degrees
BCl3 is trigonal planar: 120 degrees
NH3 is about 107 degrees and H2O about 104.5 degrees

questions.question: What are the shapes of the AlCl3 and PH3 molecules? The answer options are missing from the extracted text.
questions.answer: D: AlCl3 trigonal planar, PH3 pyramidal
steps: AlCl3: Al has 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so the shape is trigonal planar (120 degrees)
PH3: P has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, so the shape is pyramidal
Only option D gives trigonal planar for AlCl3 and pyramidal for PH3

questions.question: Boric acid contains 17.48% B, 77.67% O and the rest H. Its molar mass is 61.8 g mol-1. Show that its molecular formula is H3BO3. Ar: H = 1, B = 10.8, O = 16.
steps: Empirical formula BH3O3 has mass 61.8, equal to the molar mass, so the molecular formula is H3BO3

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of B(OH)3, showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: B in the centre bonded to three O atoms by single bonds, each O bonded to one H; no lone pairs on B; each O has two lone pairs
steps: B has 3 outer electrons, each O has 6 and each H has 1
Each O-H bond is one shared pair; each B-O bond is one shared pair
B forms three B-O bonds using its three electrons, so it has no lone pairs and no octet is needed
Each O has two lone pairs in addition to its two bonds

questions.question: Suggest a value for the O-B-O bond angle in B(OH)3 and justify it.
questions.answer: About 120 degrees
steps: B has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs
Three bonding pairs repel equally and spread to maximum separation in a plane
The shape is trigonal planar, so the O-B-O angle is 120 degrees

questions.question: What is the expected bond angle in boron trichloride, BCl3? Options: A 90 degrees, B 107 degrees, C 109.5 degrees, D 120 degrees.
questions.answer: D (120 degrees)
steps: BCl3 has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs on B
This gives a trigonal planar shape with 120 degree angles

questions.question: What is the expected bond angle in an ammonium ion? Options: A 90 degrees, B 104.5 degrees, C 107 degrees, D 109.5 degrees.
questions.answer: D (109.5 degrees)
steps: NH4+ has four bonding pairs and no lone pairs on N
Four bonding pairs repel to a tetrahedral shape with 109.5 degree angles

questions.question: What is the expected bond angle in oxygen difluoride, OF2? Options: A 90 degrees, B 104.5 degrees, C 109.5 degrees, D 180 degrees.
questions.answer: B (104.5 degrees)
steps: O has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs
Two lone pairs push the bonding pairs together, giving a bent shape
The F-O-F angle is about 104.5 degrees

questions.question: Give the electronic configuration of aluminium (atomic number 13).
steps: Aluminium has 13 electrons
Fill the subshells: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p1

questions.question: Compare and contrast the electronic structures of boron, aluminium and thallium.
questions.answer: All three have three outer electrons (ns2 np1), but B has 2 shells, Al has 3 and Tl has 6 shells; Tl also has filled 4f and 5d subshells
steps: Similarity: all three have an outer configuration ns2 np1, giving three outer electrons
Difference: boron has only two shells, aluminium has three and thallium has six
Thallium has filled 4f and 5d subshells between its core and outer shell, which boron and aluminium do not have

questions.question: Using electron pair repulsion theory, deduce the expected shape of BCl3, AlCl3 and TlCl3 and justify your answer.
questions.answer: All three are trigonal planar with Cl-M-Cl angles of 120 degrees, because each has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs on the central atom
steps: Each central atom (B, Al, Tl) has three outer electrons, all used in bonds to Cl
So each has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs
Three bonding pairs repel equally and spread out in a plane
The shape is trigonal planar with bond angles of 120 degrees for all three

questions.question: A 5.00 g sample of AlCl3 is vaporised at 455 K and 1.01 x 10^5 Pa, giving 700 cm3 of gas. Show the data are consistent with Al2Cl6 in the gas phase. R = 8.31 J mol-1 K-1.
questions.answer: n = 0.0187 mol, molar mass = 267 g mol-1, consistent with Al2Cl6 (M = 267.0)
steps: Convert volume: 700 cm3 = 7.00 x 10^-4 m3
Molar mass = mass/n = 5.00/0.0187 = 267 g mol-1
AlCl3 has M = 133.5 and Al2Cl6 has M = 267.0, so the vapour is Al2Cl6

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of Al2Cl6 using dots for aluminium electrons and crosses for chlorine electrons.
questions.answer: Two Al atoms, each bonded to four Cl atoms: two terminal Cl with normal shared pairs, and two bridging Cl atoms donating a lone pair to Al (dative bonds); each Al has 8 electrons
steps: Each Al forms two normal Al-Cl bonds to terminal Cl atoms
Each Al also accepts a lone pair from a bridging Cl, giving two dative bonds
Each Al then has 8 electrons around it, and each bridging Cl has a lone pair shared to Al

questions.question: Draw the shape of the TlCl4^3- ion, which has 10 electrons in the outer shell of thallium, and predict the bond angles, including any lone pairs that affect the shape.
questions.answer: See-saw: 4 bonding pairs + 1 lone pair (trigonal bipyramidal pair arrangement); lone pair equatorial; angles about 120 degrees (equatorial Cl-Tl-Cl, slightly less) and about 90 degrees (axial-equatorial, slightly less)
steps: Tl has 3 outer electrons, + 3 for the 3- charge, + 4 from the four Cl = 10 electrons, so 5 pairs
Four pairs are bonding pairs and one is a lone pair
Five pairs adopt a trigonal bipyramid, with the lone pair in an equatorial position (fewest 90 degree repulsions)
The shape of the ion is therefore see-saw: two axial Cl and two equatorial Cl, with Cl-Tl-Cl angles about 90 degrees (axial-equatorial) and about 120 degrees (equatorial-equatorial)
The lone pair repels more strongly than bonding pairs, so these angles are slightly smaller and the axial Cl-Tl-Cl angle is slightly less than 180 degrees

questions.question: Which molecule is polar? Options: A CO2(g), B CCl4(g), C BeCl2(g), D NH3(g).
questions.answer: D (NH3)
steps: CO2, CCl4 and BeCl2 are symmetrical, so their bond dipoles cancel
NH3 is trigonal pyramidal with a lone pair, so its bond dipoles do not cancel
NH3 therefore has a permanent dipole

questions.question: PCl5 is trigonal bipyramidal. Chlorine atoms are replaced by fluorine one at a time, axial positions first. Which product has no permanent dipole? Options: A PCl4F, B PCl3F2, C PCl2F3, D PClF4.
questions.answer: B (PCl3F2)
steps: Axial positions are replaced first, so PCl3F2 has both F atoms axial
Its three Cl atoms occupy the equatorial plane, so the two axial F atoms are opposite each other
The bond dipoles are symmetrical and cancel, so PCl3F2 has no permanent dipole
The other three products have unsymmetrical arrangements with a net dipole

questions.question: Give the name of the compound S2F10.
questions.answer: Disulfur decafluoride
steps: Prefix di means two sulfur atoms
Prefix deca means ten fluorine atoms

questions.question: S2F10 consists of two SF5 units linked by an S-S bond. Complete the dot-and-cross diagram showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: Two S atoms joined by one S-S shared pair; each S bonded to five F atoms by single bonds; no lone pairs on S; each F has three lone pairs
steps: Each S has 6 outer electrons and uses all of them in bonds
Each S forms five S-F bonds and one S-S bond, giving six bonds per S
Each F has one bond and three lone pairs

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of SF4 showing all outer shell electrons.
questions.answer: S in the centre with four single bonds to F atoms and one lone pair on S; each F has three lone pairs
steps: S has 6 outer electrons; four are used in S-F bonds
The remaining two S electrons form one lone pair
Each F has one bond and three lone pairs

questions.question: Complete the table showing the shapes of S2F10 and SF4 and their F-S-F bond angles. The table is not in the extracted text.
questions.answer: S2F10: octahedral around each S, F-S-F 90 degrees; SF4: see-saw, F-S-F about 90 degrees and about 120 degrees (both slightly less) with axial F-S-F slightly less than 180 degrees
steps: S2F10: each S has 6 bonding pairs (5 S-F + 1 S-S) and no lone pairs, so each S is octahedral; draw two octahedra sharing an S-S bond
F-S-F angle in S2F10 is 90 degrees (axial-equatorial F), as in SF6
SF4: S has 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, five pairs in a trigonal bipyramid, so the shape is see-saw (distorted tetrahedral)

SF4 angles: about 120 degrees between equatorial F (slightly less) and about 90 degrees between axial and equatorial F (slightly less), because the equatorial lone pair repels the bonding pairs more strongly

questions.question: Justify the shape around the sulfur atom in SF6 and in SF4.
questions.answer: SF6 is octahedral (six bonding pairs, no lone pairs, 90 degree angles); SF4 is see-saw (four bonding pairs and one lone pair)
steps: SF6: S has six bonding pairs and no lone pairs
Six pairs repel to an octahedral arrangement with 90 degree F-S-F angles
SF4: S has four bonding pairs and one lone pair in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement
The lone pair occupies an equatorial position, giving a see-saw shape with distorted angles

questions.question: Suggest reasons why SF4 and S2F10 are reactive but SF6 is unreactive, considering shape and bonding.
questions.answer: SF6 has six S-F bonds around S in a symmetrical octahedron, shielding S from attack; SF4 has an exposed lone pair on S; S2F10 has a weak, reactive S-S bond
steps: In SF6, the sulfur is fully surrounded by six F atoms in a symmetrical octahedron, so it is shielded from attack
SF4 has a lone pair on S that is not shielded, so it can be attacked by reagents
S2F10 contains a weaker, more reactive S-S bond that can break in reactions
